gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'Hand in your phones,' the invigilator instructed. The invigilator instructed us ___ in our phones.
gaps.explanation: Formal commands: instruct + object + to-infinitive; the particle 'in' stays with the verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I can swim,' the boy boasted. The boy boasted that he ___ swim.
gaps.explanation: Can backshifts to could in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' they asked. They ___ me to stay for dinner.
gaps.explanation: Offers of this kind are reported as invited somebody to do something.
